subject: Literacy
title: Rhyme time
subtopics: Hearing words that sound the same at the end
objectives: Children will notice when two words rhyme.
Children will finish a familiar rhyme with a rhyming word.
content: Hearing when words sound the same at the end, finishing a rhyme with a rhyming word, and matching rhyming pairs with pictures.
teachingActivities: Say rhyming pairs slowly and stretch the ending; use real objects so children can hold the pair; always pause before the rhyming word; never ask children to explain why words rhyme.
learnerActivities: Notice rhyming words, finish a familiar rhyme and match two rhyming pictures with support.
resources: Toy cat and hat, dog and log, pan and fan
assessment: Observe whether each child says the rhyming word in a familiar rhyme and matches two pictures that rhyme with support.
expectedOutcomes: Says the rhyming word in a familiar rhyme.
Matches two pictures that rhyme with support.
crossCurricular: Social Habits: listening to a friend

lessons.title: Words that sound the same
lessons.subject: Literacy
lessons.subtopic: Hearing words that sound the same at the end
objectives: Children will hear two words that rhyme and repeat them.
successCriteria: Repeats both words of a rhyming pair
Smiles or claps when words rhyme
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children know several rhymes and songs from Term 1 and can say the last word of a line when the teacher pauses.
resources: A toy cat and a toy hat
lessons.starter: Hold up the toy cat and the toy hat and say "Cat, hat. They sound the same at the end. Cat, hat."
teacherActivities: Say "cat, hat" slowly, stretching the ending "-at". Hold up each toy as you say it.
Say "cat, hat" again and clap when they rhyme.
Say "cat, dog" and shake your head. Say "cat, hat" and nod.
Let the puppet say pairs and ask "Do they sound the same?"
learnerActivities: Children copy the nod or shake of the head.
Children nod for a rhyme and shake for no rhyme.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Say "cat, hat" slowly, stretching the ending "-at". Hold up each toy as you say it. Children: Children look and repeat "cat, hat".
Step 2. Teacher: Say "cat, hat" again and clap when they rhyme. Children: Children clap with you.
Step 3. Teacher: Say "cat, dog" and shake your head. Say "cat, hat" and nod. Children: Children copy the nod or shake of the head.
Step 4. Teacher: Let the puppet say pairs and ask "Do they sound the same?" Children: Children nod for a rhyme and shake for no rhyme.

practical.title: Cat and hat
steps: Put a toy cat and a toy hat in the basket.
Each child takes one out and says its name.
The group says "cat, hat" together and claps.
practical.safety: Use clean, large toys that cannot be swallowed. Keep the basket within reach and supervise sharing.

differentiation.support: Hold the toys and say the two words slowly with the child.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to say another word that sounds like cat.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Do cat and hat sound the same?
questions.expected: Yes, with a nod or word.

questions.question: Do cat and dog sound the same?
questions.expected: No, with a shake of the head or word.

expectedOutcomes: Shows when two words rhyme with an action
lessons.conclusion: Say "cat, hat" once more and put the toys to bed.
lessons.homeConnection: Say a rhyming pair such as "cat, hat" at home and clap together.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "hear two words that rhyme and repeat them" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: Cat and hat, cat and hat, they sound the same. Cat and hat.

lessons.title: Dog and log
lessons.subject: Literacy
lessons.subtopic: Hearing words that sound the same at the end
objectives: Children will listen to more rhyming pairs and repeat them.
successCriteria: Joins in with pan and fan
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children know several rhymes and songs from Term 1 and can say the last word of a line when the teacher pauses.
resources: A toy dog and a small log or stick
A pan and a hand fan
lessons.starter: Hold up the dog and the log and say "Dog, log. They sound the same." Wag the dog.
teacherActivities: Say "dog, log" slowly and show each object.
Show the pan and the fan and say "pan, fan".
Mix the pairs: say "dog, fan" and ask "Same?"
learnerActivities: Children shake their heads for no.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Say "dog, log" slowly and show each object. Children: Children repeat the words.
Step 2. Teacher: Show the pan and the fan and say "pan, fan". Children: Children repeat the pair.
Step 3. Teacher: Mix the pairs: say "dog, fan" and ask "Same?" Children: Children shake their heads for no.
Step 4. Teacher: Say "pan, fan" and ask "Same?" Children: Children nod and clap.

practical.title: Rhyme sort
steps: Put the four objects on the mat.
Ask each child to take two that sound the same.
practical.safety: Use a smooth, short stick that is not sharp. Keep objects large and away from mouths.

differentiation.support: Use two pairs only and say the pair together.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find a rhyming pair in the classroom.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Do pan and fan sound the same?

expectedOutcomes: Picks two objects that rhyme with support
lessons.conclusion: Put each pair in the basket and say the pair.
lessons.homeConnection: Play with a pan and a fan at home and say "pan, fan".
teacherReflection: Which children could show "listen to more rhyming pairs and repeat them" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Finish the rhyme
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will finish a familiar rhyme with a rhyming word.
successCriteria: Says the last word of a rhyme
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children know several rhymes and songs from Term 1 and can say the last word of a line when the teacher pauses.
resources: Picture cards of a cat, a hat, a dog and a log
lessons.starter: Say "Cat in a hat. Cat in a" and pause. Point to the hat card.
teacherActivities: Say the rhyme "The cat sat on a hat" and "The dog sat on a log". Show the cards.
Say the rhyme again and stop before the last word.
Say it again and use the picture card as a clue if needed.
Let the puppet say a line and wait for a child to finish it.
learnerActivities: Children listen and look at the pictures.
Child says the word or points to the card.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Say the rhyme "The cat sat on a hat" and "The dog sat on a log". Show the cards. Children: Children listen and look at the pictures.
Step 2. Teacher: Say the rhyme again and stop before the last word. Children: Children say "hat" or "log".
Step 3. Teacher: Say it again and use the picture card as a clue if needed. Children: Child says the word or points to the card.
Step 4. Teacher: Let the puppet say a line and wait for a child to finish it. Children: Child finishes the rhyme.

practical.title: Puppet rhymes
steps: Sit in a circle with the puppet.
The puppet says a rhyme and pauses.
The child who is chosen finishes the rhyme.
practical.safety: Keep voices gentle and give each child time to answer. Do not hurry a shy child.

differentiation.support: Show the picture clue before the pause.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to make up a line about a cat or a dog.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: The cat sat on a what?
The dog sat on a what?

expectedOutcomes: Finishes a rhyme with the right word
lessons.conclusion: Say the two rhymes together and wave goodbye.
lessons.homeConnection: Say a simple rhyme at home and pause for your child to say the last word.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "finish a familiar rhyme with a rhyming word" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Rhyming pairs
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will match two pictures that rhyme with support.
successCriteria: Picks two pictures that sound the same
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children know several rhymes and songs from Term 1 and can say the last word of a line when the teacher pauses.
resources: Picture cards: cat, hat, dog, log, pan, fan
lessons.starter: Show the cat and hat cards and say "Cat and hat. They make a pair."
teacherActivities: Lay out the six cards face up. Pick up the cat and ask "What goes with cat?"
Say "dog" and ask "What goes with dog?"
Let each child pick a card and find its pair.
Say each pair together at the end.
learnerActivities: Child finds the pair and says the words.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Lay out the six cards face up. Pick up the cat and ask "What goes with cat?" Children: Children point to the hat.
Step 2. Teacher: Say "dog" and ask "What goes with dog?" Children: Children point to the log.
Step 3. Teacher: Let each child pick a card and find its pair. Children: Child finds the pair and says the words.
Step 4. Teacher: Say each pair together at the end. Children: Children say the pairs.

practical.title: Rhyme lotto
steps: Spread six cards on the mat.
Each child takes one card and finds the one that rhymes.
practical.safety: Use large, soft cards without sharp corners. Supervise turn-taking.

differentiation.support: Use only four cards and say the pair for the child to copy.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find all three pairs without help.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Put each pair in the basket and say goodbye.
lessons.homeConnection: Look for two things that sound the same, such as a pan and a fan, and say them together.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "match two pictures that rhyme with support" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 1 rhyme check
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child notices and finishes rhymes.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children know several rhymes and songs from Term 1 and can say the last word of a line when the teacher pauses.
lessons.starter: Sing the cat and hat song and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: finish the rhyme, rhyme lotto and puppet pairs.
At each station say a rhyme and pause, then ask "Which goes with it?"
Record each child’s level and take photographs.
learnerActivities: Child says the word or points.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: finish the rhyme, rhyme lotto and puppet pairs. Children: Children rotate every four minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station say a rhyme and pause, then ask "Which goes with it?" Children: Child says the word or points.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level and take photographs. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Rhyme stations
practical.safety: Use soft cards and toys. Supervise each station and keep floors clear.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use two pairs.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to say a new rhyming pair.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: says the rhyming word in a familiar rhyme; matches rhyming pictures; repeats a rhyming pair.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 1
lessons.conclusion: Sing the rhyme song and wave goodbye.
lessons.homeConnection: Say rhyming pairs at home and let your child finish the rhyme.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child notices and finishes rhymes" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
